To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
adolescent and young adult (AYA) patients are underrepresented in cancer clinical trials and that there are multiple barriers to AYA participation in cancer trials.

1) Adolescent and young adult patients are not being adequately referred to comprehensive cancer centers; 2) The proportion of adolescent and young adult clinical trial patients is unacceptably small; 3) There is a real gap in care for patients with certain types of cancers; 4) Adolescent and young adults are not being adequately included in the clinical trial process; 5) There are a variety of factors that influence the referral and participation of adolescent and young adults in clinical trials.

the following are the most important barriers to clinical trial participation for adolescents and young adults with cancer: (1) the lack of awareness by patients, families, and health care providers of the availability of clinical trials and the potential benefits of participation; (2) the lack of access to clinical trials for patients in this age range; and (3) a general perception by patients, families and health care providers that clinical trials are inappropriate for patients in this population.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the participation of adolescent and young adult (AYA) cancer patients in clinical research trials has been unacceptably low.
adolescent and young adult oncology is an area of medicine where there are significant gaps in our knowledge.
the current state of the science is that we do not know enough to recommend any particular strategy to increase participation of adolescent and young adults in clinical trials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a great need to increase participation of adolescents and young adults in clinical trials.
the most important factors that affect enrolment in clinical trials are not related to the patient, but to the physician and to the health care system.

the most important factor in increasing participation in clinical trials is the development of a culture in which participation in research is considered a routine and essential part of the care for cancer patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have to do a much better job of identifying patients with cancer and getting them into the appropriate treatment programs.
the most effective way to increase the number of young people in cancer clinical trials would be to increase their enrollment in clinical trials for all diseases, and not just cancer.

we need to be more aggressive in identifying and referring patients to clinical trials, particularly those who are at high risk for developing a recurrence or a second cancer, and we need to be creative in designing trials for these patients.
